title: Every prime of a finite product comes from one factor
statement: Let $I$ be a finite index set, let $(R_i)_{i\in I}$ be commutative rings, and put $R=\prod_{i\in I}R_i$. For every point $\mathfrak p$ of $\operatorname{Spec}R$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], that is, every prime ideal of $R$, there are $i\in I$ and a prime ideal $\mathfrak q$ of $R_i$ such that $\mathfrak p=\pi_i^{-1}(\mathfrak q)$, where $\pi_i:R\to R_i$ is the coordinate projection. In particular, when $I$ is empty, $R$ has no prime ideals.
